::: {.callout-important}
Partly implemented. The Phase 1 surface is served today — 93 operations over 70 paths, all of them
in [`spec/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/openapi.yaml),
which is the authority. Anything on this page that the committed document does not declare belongs
to a later phase and is intent, not contract.
:::

**Nothing in Recueil is UI-only.** That is a binding principle rather than an aspiration, and it has
a test: if a feature can be done in the web interface and not through the API, the feature is not
finished. The web UI, the CLI, the MCP server and the R and Python packages are all clients of the
same endpoints, with no privileged back channel between the UI and the server.

## The contract

`spec/openapi.yaml` is generated from the Zod schemas the server validates with, so the document and
the implementation cannot drift: they are the same source. OpenAPI 3.1, versioned under `/api/v1`.

The generated document drives the TypeScript client, the Python models, the MCP tool definitions and
the reference section of this site.

## Authentication

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RECUEIL_TOKEN" \
     https://recueil.example.org/api/v1/items?limit=25
```

Scoped bearer tokens for programmatic access, session cookies for the browser. Scopes are
resource-and-verb pairs (`items:read`, `sr:write`, `admin:*`). Every mutation is attributed in the
audit log to the token that made it.

## Resources

| Group | Paths | What lives there |
|---|---|---|
| Library | `/items`, `/documents`, `/attachments`, `/collections`, `/tags`, `/fields`, `/notes`, `/annotations`, `/creators`, `/terms` | The core model |
| Search | `/search` | Boolean and per-field queries, facets, saved searches |
| Graph | `/graph/nodes`, `/graph/edges`, `/graph/deep-dive` | Citation and derived networks, shadow works, budgeted expansion |
| Analytics | `/analytics/export` | Parquet bundle for R, Python and DuckDB |
| Quality | `/checks`, `/dedup` | The verification engine and both dedup layers, including dry runs |
| Ingestion | `/ingestion/sources`, `/ingestion/queue`, `/ingestion/review` | Sources, the pipeline and the review queue |
| Systematic review | `/sr/reviews`, `/sr/screening`, `/sr/extraction`, `/sr/rob`, `/sr/prisma` | The PRISMA workflow |
| Networks | `/networks` | Curated network documents, versions, freezing |
| Platform | `/plugins`, `/jobs`, `/export`, `/system` | Administration |

## Conventions

**Pagination** is cursor-based for records. Offsets lie when the underlying set changes under you,
and analytics should not be paginated at all — that is what the Parquet export is for.

**Bulk endpoints** take an array and an `Idempotency-Key` header. Replaying a key returns the
original result rather than acting twice, which is what makes a client-side write queue safe.

**Errors** are RFC 9457 problem documents: a stable `type` URI, a human `title`, and a `detail` that
names the field.

**Events** arrive on an SSE stream at `/events`, filtered by type, and as outbound webhooks with an
HMAC signature. The event vocabulary is the same one plugins subscribe to: `item.created`,
`item.updated`, `item.merged`, `document.ingested`, `check.completed`, `job.finished`, and the rest
of the [hook catalogue](plugins.qmd).

## Analytics: tables, not JSON

Bibliometrics needs columns. Paginating a hundred thousand works through JSON to build a co-citation
matrix is the wrong shape of pipe, so there is a second one ([ADR-0008](adr.qmd)).

```sh
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RECUEIL_TOKEN" \
     "https://recueil.example.org/api/v1/analytics/export?collection=phd" \
     -o export.zip
```

The bundle contains Parquet files — `works`, `creators`, `works_creators`, `terms`, `works_terms`,
`edges`, `metrics`, and the systematic-review tables — which Arrow, polars, pandas and DuckDB all
read natively. In local mode, DuckDB can attach the SQLite file directly and skip the export.

Converters produce the formats the analysis ecosystem already expects: a bibliometrix `M` data frame
with Web of Science tag mapping (`AU`, `AF`, `TI`, `SO`, `DT`, `DE`, `ID`, `AB`, `C1`, `CR`, `TC`,
`PY`, `DI`, `SR`), VOSviewer network and map JSON, Gephi GEXF, GraphML, CiteSpace WoS text, and CSV.

## MCP

The MCP server exposes the API to language models as tools derived from the same OpenAPI document:
search, get, add and update items, run checks, dry-run dedup, launch a deep dive, export BibTeX,
record screening decisions, write extraction data. Resources cover library statistics and review
status; prompts cover reference auditing and screening assistance.

Writes made through MCP are attributed in the audit log exactly like any other token, and are
scoped by that token. A model gets the permissions you gave it and no others, and you can see
afterwards what it did. For systematic reviews there is a further control: automation disclosure is
a per-review setting that records which decisions were tool-assisted, off by default, exported with
the audit trail when on ([ADR-0020](adr.qmd)).

## Connector endpoint

`/connector/*` implements Zotero's connector protocol, so the existing Zotero Connector extension
and its translator library work against Recueil unmodified ([ADR-0006](adr.qmd)). Recueil ships its
own WebExtension in Phase 8, speaking the same protocol with a collection and tag picker,
office-document capture and page snapshots.

## Clients

| Client | Language | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `@recueil/client-ts` | TypeScript | Generated from the OpenAPI document; used by the web UI |
| `recueil` | R | `httr2`. `rc_items()`, `rc_search()`, `rc_bibtex()`, `rc_analytics()`, `rc_bibliometrix()` → an `M` data frame that runs in biblioshiny unmodified, `rc_graph()` → tidygraph, `rc_sr_*()`, `rc_checks()`. Separate repository, CRAN-bound |
| `recueil` | Python | `httpx`, typed models from OpenAPI, polars and pandas frames, networkx and igraph graphs. Separate repository, PyPI-bound |
| `recueil` | CLI | See [the CLI page](cli.qmd) |

## Citation endpoints

Per-collection and per-saved-search `.bib` URLs, with a scoped token in the URL, so Overleaf, Quarto
and Pandoc can pull a bibliography that is never stale. Citation keys are stable, pinned per item
and Better BibTeX-compatible by default ([ADR-0016](adr.qmd)), so a `.bib` that regenerates does not
break the `\cite` commands in your manuscript.

CSL-JSON, BibTeX and BibLaTeX, RIS and JSON-LD are available for everything, at every scope.
